scf.controlDescription: Access to Azure subscription management must be restricted. Owner role assignments should not exceed 3 principals to limit blast radius from compromised accounts.

cmmc.title: Limit system access to authorized users and enforce least privilege

impactRating.rationale: Excessive Owner assignments violate least privilege and expand the attack surface for subscription takeover.

scf.controlDescription: Azure subscriptions must have at least one resource lock configured to prevent accidental or unauthorized deletion or modification of critical resources.

cmmc.title: Establish and enforce security configuration settings

impactRating.rationale: Absence of locks allows accidental or malicious deletion of production resources with no rollback protection.

scf.controlDescription: Azure Policy compliance must be reviewed manually in the Portal to confirm that assigned policies are not generating non-compliant findings against baseline configurations.

cmmc.title: Establish and maintain baseline configurations and inventories

impactRating.rationale: Unreviewed policy non-compliance indicates configuration drift from the security baseline.

name: Guest User Count in Azure AD

scf.controlDescription: Guest user accounts in Azure AD should be reviewed and minimized. External identities with persistent access to Azure resources increase the risk of unauthorized access.

cmmc.title: Limit system access to authorized users

impactRating.rationale: Guest accounts are often over-privileged and rarely reviewed, creating persistent unauthorized access paths.

scf.controlDescription: Service principal credentials (client secrets and certificates) must not be expired. Expired credentials indicate abandoned applications or poor credential lifecycle management.

cmmc.title: Authenticate the identities of users, processes, and devices

impactRating.rationale: Expired credentials on active service principals indicate unmanaged automation that may have been compromised or abandoned.

scf.controlDescription: Azure resources should use managed identities instead of service principals with stored secrets where possible, reducing credential exposure and enforcing least-privilege identity patterns.

cmmc.title: Employ the principle of least privilege

impactRating.rationale: Service principals with stored secrets are a common attack vector; managed identities eliminate secret management overhead.

scf.controlDescription: Network Security Groups must not allow inbound RDP (TCP 3389) from any internet source (0.0.0.0/0, *, or Internet). Unrestricted RDP exposure is a primary vector for brute-force and ransomware attacks.

cmmc.title: Monitor, control, and protect organizational communications

impactRating.rationale: Internet-exposed RDP is consistently exploited for ransomware deployment and lateral movement.

scf.controlDescription: Network Security Groups must not allow inbound SSH (TCP 22) from any internet source. Unrestricted SSH exposure enables brute-force credential attacks against Linux VMs.

cmmc.title: Monitor, control, and protect organizational communications

impactRating.rationale: Internet-exposed SSH is a top attack vector for Linux VM compromise and cryptomining deployments.

scf.controlDescription: VMs with public IP addresses must each have an associated NSG. Review all public-IP VMs to verify the exposure is intentional and protected.

cmmc.title: Monitor, control, and protect organizational communications

impactRating.rationale: Public IPs without NSGs expose the VM attack surface directly to the internet.

scf.controlDescription: Storage accounts must not allow anonymous (unauthenticated) access to blob containers. Public blob access exposes potentially sensitive data to the internet without any authentication.

cmmc.title: Employ architectural designs and implement security functionality

impactRating.rationale: Public blob containers have caused numerous data breaches through accidental exposure of sensitive files.

scf.controlDescription: All storage accounts must enforce HTTPS-only traffic to protect data in transit. HTTP connections must be rejected to prevent interception of data or credentials.

cmmc.title: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure

impactRating.rationale: Unencrypted HTTP transfers can expose storage access keys and data to network-level interception.

scf.controlDescription: Storage accounts must enforce TLS 1.2 as the minimum version. TLS 1.0 and 1.1 have known vulnerabilities (POODLE, BEAST) that can be exploited to decrypt communications.

cmmc.title: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure

impactRating.rationale: TLS 1.0/1.1 vulnerabilities allow downgrade attacks against storage communications.

scf.controlDescription: Azure Key Vaults must have soft delete enabled to allow recovery of accidentally or maliciously deleted secrets, keys, and certificates within the retention period.

cmmc.title: Employ FIPS-validated cryptography

impactRating.rationale: Without soft delete, a deleted Key Vault permanently destroys all cryptographic material, potentially causing application outages.

scf.controlDescription: Azure Key Vaults must have purge protection enabled to prevent permanent deletion during the soft-delete retention period, protecting against ransomware-style attacks targeting cryptographic material.

cmmc.title: Employ FIPS-validated cryptography

impactRating.rationale: Without purge protection, an attacker with Key Vault delete permissions can permanently destroy all secrets, keys, and certificates.

name: Key Vault Keys and Secrets Expiry Configured

scf.controlDescription: Cryptographic keys and secrets stored in Azure Key Vault must have expiry dates configured to enforce key rotation and reduce the window of exposure if a key is compromised.

cmmc.title: Store and transmit only cryptographically-protected passwords

impactRating.rationale: Keys without expiry never rotate, allowing long-term exploitation of any compromise without detection.

scf.controlDescription: Microsoft Defender for Cloud paid plans (Servers, Databases, Storage, etc.) must be enabled to provide threat detection, vulnerability assessment, and security recommendations for CUI-handling workloads.

cmmc.title: Scan for vulnerabilities in organizational systems

impactRating.rationale: Without paid Defender plans, threat detection and vulnerability scanning are absent for critical workloads.

name: Defender for Cloud Secure Score Threshold

scf.controlDescription: The Defender for Cloud Secure Score must meet a minimum threshold (>=50%) to indicate that foundational security recommendations have been addressed across the subscription.

cmmc.title: Scan for vulnerabilities in organizational systems

impactRating.rationale: A low secure score indicates widespread unresolved security findings that increase risk of compromise.

scf.controlDescription: Defender for Cloud auto-provisioning of monitoring agents (MMA/AMA) must be enabled to ensure all VMs automatically receive threat detection coverage without manual intervention.

cmmc.title: Monitor organizational systems to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks

impactRating.rationale: VMs without monitoring agents are invisible to Defender for Cloud threat detection.

scf.controlDescription: At least one Log Analytics workspace must exist in the subscription to serve as a central repository for audit logs, diagnostic data, and security events.

cmmc.title: Create and retain system audit logs to enable monitoring, analysis, investigation, and reporting

impactRating.rationale: Without a Log Analytics workspace, audit log collection cannot be centralized, making incident investigation impossible.

name: Activity Log Alert for Delete Policy Assignment

scf.controlDescription: An enabled Activity Log Alert must exist for the Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments/delete operation to detect and respond to unauthorized removal of security policies.

cmmc.title: Correlate audit record review, analysis, and reporting processes

impactRating.rationale: Silent policy deletion can remove compliance guardrails without anyone noticing until the next audit.

name: Azure Disk Encryption Extension on All VMs

scf.controlDescription: All virtual machines must have the Azure Disk Encryption extension installed and in a Succeeded provisioning state to protect OS and data disks with BitLocker (Windows) or dm-crypt (Linux).

cmmc.title: Protect the confidentiality of CUI at rest

impactRating.rationale: Unencrypted VM disks expose CUI if the underlying hardware is repurposed or physically accessed.

name: Endpoint Protection Extension on All VMs

scf.controlDescription: All virtual machines must have an endpoint protection extension installed (Microsoft Antimalware or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint) to detect and prevent malicious code execution.

cmmc.title: Provide protection from malicious code at appropriate locations within organizational systems

impactRating.rationale: VMs without endpoint protection are undefended against malware, ransomware, and fileless attacks.

scf.controlDescription: All Azure SQL databases (excluding system databases) must have Transparent Data Encryption enabled to protect database files, log files, and backups at rest.

cmmc.title: Protect the confidentiality of CUI at rest

impactRating.rationale: Unencrypted SQL databases expose CUI stored in database files and backups.

scf.controlDescription: SQL Server auditing must be enabled on all Azure SQL servers to track database events, schema changes, and data access for compliance and incident investigation.

cmmc.title: Create and retain system audit logs

impactRating.rationale: Without auditing, SQL Server access and schema changes are untracked and cannot be investigated after a breach.

name: SQL Server Firewall Rules Not Overly Permissive

scf.controlDescription: Azure SQL Server firewall rules must not allow unrestricted access from all Azure services (0.0.0.0-0.0.0.0) or from the entire internet (0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255).

cmmc.title: Monitor, control, and protect organizational communications

impactRating.rationale: Overly broad SQL firewall rules expose the database server to unauthorized connection attempts from anywhere in Azure or the internet.

scf.controlDescription: All AKS clusters must have Kubernetes RBAC enabled to enforce role-based access control on Kubernetes API operations and prevent unauthorized access to cluster resources.

cmmc.title: Limit system access to the types of transactions and functions authorized users are permitted to execute

impactRating.rationale: Without RBAC, all authenticated users have unrestricted access to Kubernetes API operations including cluster-admin capabilities.

scf.controlDescription: AKS clusters must have a network policy (Azure or Calico) configured to control pod-to-pod traffic and enforce microsegmentation within the cluster.

cmmc.title: Monitor, control, and protect organizational communications

impactRating.rationale: Without network policies, a compromised pod can communicate freely with all other pods, enabling lateral movement.

scf.controlDescription: AKS clusters must have Azure AD integration (AAD profile or OIDC issuer) enabled to enforce organizational identity policies, MFA, and conditional access for cluster authentication.

cmmc.title: Identify information system users, processes acting on behalf of users, and devices

impactRating.rationale: Without Azure AD integration, AKS authentication relies on local credentials that bypass organizational MFA and conditional access policies.
